games.title: Steroid and Sex Hormones: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 2 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which of the following is the primary androgen produced by the fetal adrenal gland during the first trimester?
questions.explanation: DHEAS is the main adrenal androgen secreted in early pregnancy.

questions.q: A 28‑year‑old woman presents with hirsutism and irregular menses. Serum LH:FSH ratio is 4:1. Which hormone is most likely elevated?
questions.explanation: An LH:FSH ratio >2:1 suggests excess LH, typical of PCOS.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a direct metabolite of testosterone in the liver?
questions.explanation: Cortisol is not a testosterone metabolite; it is a glucocorticoid.

questions.q: A patient with congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21‑hydroxylase deficiency has markedly elevated levels of which precursor?
questions.explanation: 17‑Hydroxyprogesterone accumulates when 21‑hydroxylase is deficient.

questions.q: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the development of female secondary sexual characteristics during puberty?
questions.explanation: Estradiol drives breast development, body hair, and menstrual cycle onset.

questions.q: Which of the following is a potent inhibitor of 5α‑reductase, thereby reducing dihydrotestosterone formation?
questions.explanation: Finasteride blocks 5α‑reductase, lowering DHT levels.

questions.q: In a male patient, a serum testosterone level of 0.3 nmol/L is considered below the normal range. Which of the following is the most likely clinical consequence?
questions.explanation: Low testosterone leads to hypogonadism with fatigue, decreased libido, etc.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most sensitive assay for measuring adrenal androgen excess?
questions.explanation: LC‑MS/MS provides the most accurate measurement of adrenal androgens.

questions.q: Which hormone is synthesized from cholesterol in the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex?
questions.explanation: Aldosterone is produced in the zona glomerulosa; cortisol is from the fasciculata.

games.title: Vasculitides: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most common systemic vasculitis in adults?
questions.explanation: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is the most frequently encountered systemic vasculitis in adults, particularly those over 50 years of age.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old man presents with fever, weight loss, and palpable purpura on the lower limbs. His skin biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposition. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: IgA deposition in leukocytoclastic vasculitis is characteristic of Henoch–Schönlein purpura.

questions.q: Which antibody is most strongly associated with microscopic polyangiitis?
questions.explanation: Anti‑myeloperoxidase (MPO) antibodies are most commonly seen in microscopic polyangiitis.

questions.q: A patient with polyarteritis nodosa has livedo reticularis and mononeuritis multiplex. Which organ is least likely to be involved?
questions.explanation: Polyarteritis nodosa rarely involves the brain; it mainly affects medium‑sized arteries of kidney, heart, skin, and nerves.

questions.q: Which imaging modality is best for detecting aneurysms in polyarteritis nodosa?
questions.explanation: CT angiography is the gold standard for visualising medium‑sized arterial aneurysms in PAN.

questions.q: A 30‑year‑old woman with relapsing polychondritis develops sudden visual loss. Which vasculitis is most likely responsible for her ocular involvement?
questions.explanation: Giant cell arteritis commonly causes anterior ischemic optic neuropathy leading to sudden visual loss.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of granulomatosis with polyangiitis?
questions.explanation: Chronic hepatitis B infection is not characteristic of GPA; it is more associated with polyarteritis nodosa.

questions.q: A 55‑year‑old man with fever, abdominal pain, and hypertension is found to have microaneurysms on mesenteric angiography. Which vasculitis is most likely?
questions.explanation: Mesenteric microaneurysms are classic for polyarteritis nodosa.

questions.q: Which of the following laboratory findings is most characteristic of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg–Strauss)?
questions.explanation: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis typically shows markedly elevated serum IgE.

questions.q: A patient with systemic lupus erythematosus develops livedo reticularis and peripheral neuropathy. Which vasculitis is most likely secondary to SLE?
questions.explanation: Cutaneous small‑vessel vasculitis is the most common vasculitic manifestation in SLE.

games.title: Wk 7 liver cirrosis: case showdown
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 58‑year‑old man with a 30‑year history of alcohol abuse presents with jaundice, ascites and asterixis. His serum bilirubin is 12 mg/dL, albumin 2.8 g/dL, INR 1.8 and platelets 90 × 10^9/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The presence of ascites, jaundice, coagulopathy and thrombocytopenia indicates decompensated cirrhosis.

questions.q: A 62‑year‑old woman with known hepatitis C cirrhosis develops sudden onset confusion and asterixis. Her ammonia level is 120 µmol/L. What is the next best step?
questions.explanation: Elevated ammonia and clinical hepatic encephalopathy are first managed with lactulose to reduce ammonia production and absorption.

questions.q: A 55‑year‑old man with cirrhosis presents with a sudden drop in hemoglobin and a large, painless, palpable spleen. Which complication is most likely?
questions.explanation: In cirrhosis, a sudden fall in hemoglobin together with splenomegaly most often reflects an acute variceal hemorrhage, which can cause rapid blood loss and anemia.

questions.q: A 48‑year‑old woman with cirrhosis has a platelet count of 70 × 10^9/L and a normal coagulation profile. What is the most appropriate management?
questions.explanation: Mild thrombocytopenia in cirrhosis is usually well tolerated; transfusion is reserved for active bleeding or invasive procedures.

questions.q: A 60‑year‑old man with cirrhosis presents with a sudden onset of right upper quadrant pain and a tender, enlarged liver. His AST is 400 U/L and ALT 350 U/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Marked elevation of AST and ALT in a cirrhotic patient with recent heavy alcohol intake points to acute alcoholic hepatitis.

questions.q: A 65‑year‑old man with cirrhosis and a history of variceal bleeding is being considered for endoscopic therapy. Which endoscopic procedure is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) is the first‑line endoscopic treatment for esophageal varices to prevent re‑bleeding.

questions.q: A 52‑year‑old woman with cirrhosis develops a sudden, severe headache and vomiting. CT brain shows a subarachnoid hemorrhage. Which underlying condition is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Cirrhosis can cause a complex coagulopathy that predisposes to spontaneous intracranial bleeding such as subarachnoid hemorrhage.

questions.q: A 70‑year‑old man with cirrhosis presents with worsening renal function, oliguria and a serum creatinine of 3.0 mg/dL. His urine sodium is 10 mmol/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Low urine sodium and oliguria in the setting of advanced cirrhosis are characteristic of hepatorenal syndrome, a functional renal failure.

games.title: Obesity Types, Causes and Treatments: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which drug is a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that promotes weight loss by delaying gastric emptying and reducing appetite?
questions.explanation: Liraglutide activates GLP‑1 receptors, slows gastric emptying and suppresses appetite, leading to weight loss.

questions.q: Which mechanism is most characteristic of Orlistat in the treatment of obesity?
questions.explanation: Orlistat inhibits gastric and pancreatic lipases, preventing fat absorption.

questions.q: A patient with obesity and type 2 diabetes is started on a drug that reduces hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity. Which drug is this?
questions.explanation: Pioglitazone is a thiazolidinedione that activates PPAR‑γ, reducing hepatic gluconeogenesis and enhancing insulin sensitivity.

questions.q: Which side effect is most commonly associated with long‑term use of Orlistat?
questions.explanation: Orlistat causes steatorrhea, oily stools, and flatulence due to fat malabsorption.

questions.q: Which drug is a sympathomimetic amine that increases norepinephrine release and is used for short‑term obesity management?
questions.explanation: Phentermine is a sympathomimetic that releases norepinephrine, suppressing appetite for short‑term use.

questions.q: Which drug class is primarily indicated for patients with obesity and non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) due to its effect on weight and liver enzymes?
questions.explanation: GLP‑1 agonists like semaglutide reduce weight and improve liver enzymes in NAFLD.

questions.q: Which of the following is a contraindication for the use of Orlistat?
questions.explanation: Orlistat is contraindicated in chronic pancreatitis because it inhibits pancreatic lipase, worsening fat digestion.

games.title: MBPL3822 Chemotherapy CAT 1: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which class of drugs does MBPL3822 Chemotherapy CAT 1 belong to?
questions.explanation: MBPL3822 is an alkylating agent that cross‑links DNA.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of MBPL3822?
options: DNA cross‑linking leading to strand breaks
questions.explanation: It cross‑links DNA, preventing replication and transcription.

questions.q: For which malignancy is MBPL3822 most commonly indicated?
questions.explanation: It is primarily used in AML protocols.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic side effect of MBPL3822?
questions.explanation: Hematologic suppression (neutropenia) is the hallmark toxicity.

questions.q: MBPL3822 is metabolised predominantly by which pathway?
questions.explanation: It undergoes hepatic glucuronidation.

questions.q: Which laboratory value is most likely to be abnormal during MBPL3822 therapy?
questions.explanation: Thrombocytopenia is a common cytopenia.

questions.q: What is the recommended dose‑adjustment strategy for a patient with renal impairment receiving MBPL3822?
questions.explanation: Dose is reduced by 50% in moderate renal impairment.

questions.q: Which supportive medication is routinely co‑administered with MBPL3822 to mitigate its side effects?
questions.explanation: G‑CSF is used to prevent severe neutropenia.
